evidence: The films were grown on glass substrates (Corning 1737) for Hall measurements and X-ray diffraction (XRD). For X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS) and secondary-ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS) analysis, the films were deposited on Al2O3 (50 nm)/Si (001) substrates. The thickness of the films was routinely measured by ellipsometer (Rudolph auto ELII). The microstructure of ALD ZnO was analyzed by XRD (Rigaku Rint2500). The resistivity and Hall mobility of ZnO thin films were measured by a Hall measurement system. The microstructure of ALD ZnO was analyzed by XRD (Rigaku Rint2500). The resistivity and Hall mobility of ZnO thin films were measured by a Hall measurement system, which could measure the electrical properties of samples up to 20 G. The device characteristics, including transfer and output curves, were measured by a semiconductor parameter analyzer (Keithley 4200) with three probes. The changes in transfer curves were measured to investigate the changes in the threshold voltage and subthreshold swing. The output curves of all ZnO:N TFTs were measured at VDS = 0–20 V with VG = 20 V. The transfer curves (VG vs IDS plot) under the constant VDS of the undoped and nitrogen-doped ZnO TFTs were measured. The saturation mobilities were calculated by Eq. 1. The subthreshold swing (S) of ZnO:N TFTs was measured. The threshold voltage (Vth) was obtained by fitting the straight line of the square root of IDS vs VG. The positive gate bias stress stability was investigated by applying a gate bias of 15 V for 3600 s. The output curves of ALD ZnO:N TFTs were measured as a function of bias stress time. The threshold voltage change and subthreshold swing as a function of stress time were measured. The transfer curve of ALD ZnO:N TFTs fabricated on the PEN substrate was measured.
